title: Amiga August 2026 Update
content_html:
August 4, 2026

New agreements establish a clear framework for Commodore and Amiga technology, supporting AmigaOS development, preservation, and new projects by Amiga and its licensees

Amiga Corporation today announced two agreements concluded within a few weeks of one another. Amiga and Commodore International Corporation have entered into a licensing agreement recognizing their respective rights. Separately, a settlement with Hyperion Entertainment BV resolves a contractual dispute and replaces its 2009 agreement with Amiga.

The agreements complement other rights and arrangements, some of which Amiga can now bring into active use.

The Commodore Agreement and History

Amiga Corporation holds the registered and unregistered copyrights in the works of the former Commodore and Amiga companies. These include source code and binaries for CBM 8-bit and Amiga software and firmware, together with hardware designs, manufacturing data, documentation, marketing assets, and other materials. Amiga also owns the Amiga trademarks. The chain of title includes rights previously preserved and consolidated by Cloanto, together with additional rights acquired from other sources.

Following the 1996 liquidation of Escom, one of Amiga's predecessors in interest, the "Commodore" and "C=" trademarks took a separate path from the other assets. Tulip Computers acquired the trademarks and used them for Commodore-branded PCs. Subsequent transfers brought the trademarks to the present Commodore company. In the agreement, Amiga recognizes this ownership. The copyrights in the historical software, documentation, and other Commodore and Amiga works remained in the chain of title now continued by Amiga. Under the same agreement, Amiga licenses CBM 8-bit software and documentation to Commodore for use in its products.

Amiga retains the right to use and reproduce the Commodore marks in historical and descriptive contexts, including as they appear in original software, documentation, notices, keyboard symbols, on-screen texts, and other content.

The agreement further confirms Amiga's continuing control of technical and numbering resources historically associated with Commodore-Amiga, Commodore Business Machines, Commodore Electronics, Commodore International, and other now-defunct Commodore-formative entities: MAC address OUIs, IP address allocations, port numbers, object identifiers, and other assignments used by Amiga and its predecessors in connection with their systems and activities.

In August 1984, Commodore and Amiga brought their efforts together under Commodore-Amiga, Inc., a name Amiga Corporation still uses as a registered DBA. Forty-two years later, the circle is closing: apart from the "Commodore" and "C=" marks, the principal rights and assets of the Commodore and Amiga eras rest with Amiga.

AmigaOS 4 and 68K Continuity

The settlement agreement confirms that Hyperion Entertainment will continue to develop and distribute AmigaOS 4 under license from Amiga. The rights in the independently developed AmigaOS 4 code have never been disputed, and the new agreement preserves that position while clearly defining the Amiga software and trademarks licensed for continued AmigaOS 4 development and commercialization.

The position concerning 68K AmigaOS products is different. Under the agreement, Hyperion Entertainment's rights in that field are transitional and limited to AmigaOS 3.2 and AmigaOS 3.3 as upgrades for existing licensed systems. Distribution of those products will end no later than December 31, 2027. Amiga will continue to direct the development and evolution of AmigaOS for the 68K platform, carrying forward the lineage established by Commodore-Amiga in the 1980s.

Hyperion Entertainment will deliver to Amiga the source code, revision history, and documentation for AmigaOS 3.1.4, including all fixes and updates, but excluding AmigaOS 4 code backported into AmigaOS 3.2 or 3.3, for use in Amiga's 68K AmigaOS development. The agreement also provides for the company's contractors and developers to be released from any obligations that would prevent them from working with Amiga. Developers whose commitment has always been to AmigaOS are therefore free to contribute to its future.

Preservation and the Future

Amiga regards the preservation of historical Commodore and Amiga assets and continued development as complementary responsibilities. Its work includes identifying, securing, cataloging, and preserving source code, binaries, documentation, artwork, photos, videos, corporate records, and other materials, while maintaining lawful paths for their continued use, study, and development.

Amiga is working with preservationists, former employees, other original contributors, and cultural, educational, and research institutions, including libraries, museums, and archives.

For example, Amiga is now in a position to restore the iconic SoftVoice speech synthesis to AmigaOS. Several versions of the historic Boing Ball demo are also being prepared for release.

Amiga means different things to different people. For some, it represents an important part of computing history. For others, it remains a living platform. Preserving the past, making it accessible, and advancing the platform are central to Amiga's purpose.

Community, Projects, and Partners

Community and technology define Amiga in equal measure. Amiga's identity and direction are shaped by the diversity of its people, ideas, and projects, a shared passion for the platform, and a commitment to beauty and excellence.

Amiga supports this ecosystem by licensing its technology and trademarks for hardware and software products, publications, events, and other projects. These partnerships help high-quality work reach broad audiences and make the past, present, and future of CBM 8-bit and Amiga systems more accessible.

Current licensees include A1200.NET, Antstream Arcade, Blaze Entertainment, Cloanto, Commodore, Hyperion Entertainment (and its sublicensees), Retro Games, Simulant Systems, and SpecNext.

Amiga has already concluded additional agreements, and others are in progress. Each will be announced, with the licensees and projects listed on a renewed Amiga website.

这些协议补充了其他权利和安排，其中一些 Amiga 现在可以积极使用。

准将协议和历史

Amiga Corporation 拥有前 Commodore 和 Amiga 公司作品的注册和未注册版权。 其中包括 CBM 8 位和 Amiga 软件和固件的源代码和二进制文件，以及硬件设计、制造数据、文档、营销资产和其他材料。 Amiga 还拥有 Amiga 商标。 所有权链包括 Cloanto 先前保留和合并的权利，以及从其他来源获得的附加权利。

1996 年，Amiga 的前身之一 Escom 清算后，“Commodore”和“C=”商标与其他资产分开了。 Tulip Computers 获得了这些商标并将其用于 Commodore 品牌的个人电脑。 随后的转让将商标带到了现在的 Commodore 公司。 在协议中，Amiga 承认这种所有权。 历史软件、文档以及其他 Commodore 和 Amiga 作品的版权仍然保留在所有权链中，现在由 Amiga 延续。 根据同一协议，Amiga 向 Commodore 授权 CBM 8 位软件和文档在其产品中使用。

Amiga 保留在历史和描述性上下文中使用和复制 Commodore 标记的权利，包括它们出现在原始软件、文档、通知、键盘符号、屏幕文本和其他内容中的情况。

该协议进一步确认 Amiga 对历史上与 Commodore-Amiga、Commodore Business Machines、Commodore Electronics、Commodore International 和其他现已解散的 Commodore 形成实体相关的技术和编号资源的持续控制：MAC 地址 OUI、IP 地址分配、端口号、对象标识符以及 Amiga 及其前身在其系统和活动中使用的其他分配。

1984 年 8 月，Commodore 和 Amiga 共同成立了 Commodore-Amiga, Inc.，Amiga Corporation 至今仍使用该名称作为注册 DBA。 四十二年后，这个循环正在闭合：除了“Commodore”和“C=”标记之外，Commodore 和 Amiga 时代的主要权利和资产都属于 Amiga。

AmigaOS 4 和 68K 连续性

和解协议确认 Hyperion Entertainment 将在 Amiga 的许可下继续开发和分销 AmigaOS 4。 独立开发的AmigaOS 4代码的权利从未有过争议，新协议保留了这一立场，同时明确定义了Amiga软件和授权用于继续AmigaOS 4开发和商业化的商标。

对于68K AmigaOS 产品的立场有所不同。 根据协议，Hyperion Entertainment 在该领域的权利是过渡性的，仅限于 AmigaOS 3.2 和 AmigaOS 3.3，作为现有许可系统的升级。 这些产品的分销将在 2027 年 12 月 31 日之前结束。 Amiga 将继续指导 68K 平台 AmigaOS 的开发和演进，继承 Commodore-Amiga 在 1980 年代建立的血统。

Hyperion Entertainment 将向 Amiga 提供 AmigaOS 3.1.4 的源代码、修订历史记录和文档，包括所有修复和更新，但不包括反向移植到 AmigaOS 3.2 或 3.3 中的 AmigaOS 4 代码，以用于 Amiga 的 68K AmigaOS 开发。 该协议还规定该公司的承包商和开发商免除任何妨碍他们与 Amiga 合作的义务。 因此，始终致力于 AmigaOS 的开发人员可以自由地为其未来做出贡献。

保护与未来

Amiga 将保护 Commodore 和 Amiga 的历史资产以及持续发展视为互补的责任。 其工作包括识别、保护、编目和保存源代码、二进制文件、文档、艺术品、照片、视频、公司记录和其他材料，同时维护其继续使用、研究和开发的合法途径。

Amiga 正在与保护主义者、前雇员、其他原始贡献者以及文化、教育和研究机构（包括图书馆、博物馆和档案馆）合作。

例如，Amiga 现在可以将标志性的 SoftVoice 语音合成功能恢复到 AmigaOS 中。 历史悠久的 Boing Ball 演示版的多个版本也正在准备发布。

Amiga 对于不同的人来说意味着不同的东西。 对于某些人来说，它代表了计算历史的重要组成部分。 对于其他人来说，它仍然是一个生活平台。 保护过去、使其易于理解并推进平台的发展是 Amiga 的核心目标。

社区、项目和合作伙伴

社区和技术同等重要地定义了 Amiga。 Amiga 的身份和方向是由其人员、想法和项目的多样性、对平台的共同热情以及对美丽和卓越的承诺塑造的。

Amiga 通过授权其硬件和软件产品、出版物、活动和其他项目的技术和商标来支持这个生态系统。 这些合作伙伴关系有助于高质量的作品惠及广大受众，并使 CBM 8 位和 Amiga 系统的过去、现在和未来变得更容易理解。

目前的被许可方包括 A1200.NET、Antstream Arcade、Blaze Entertainment、Cloanto、Commodore、Hyperion Entertainment（及其分许可方）、Retro Games、Simulant Systems 和 SpecNext。

Amiga 已经达成了其他协议，其他协议正在进行中。 每一项都将在更新的 Amiga 网站上公布，并列出被许可人和项目。
